issues.quote: It tested the program's own contact-range gate.
issues.problem: This is the draft's only account of what the obituary covers, and it describes only the particle leg (Debt 3a's 10^28–10^31 shortfall). The record's verdict rests on three legs: 'nowhere mandatory — forbidden (particles), fatal (committed wave), decorative (free wave)'. On the free-wave branch (Scenario B) the record still allows streams, but at a strength tunable over ~10 orders: 'optional, never required'. #11 §15 lists this as a quarantined degeneration risk. To weigh 'premature', Paul needs to know that the obituary kills clumping as a required prediction, not as a possibility. The sentence itself is true (all three legs use the contact gate). The critic's Q1 ruling has the same omission, and the recommended 'scope sentence' for the obituary page would inherit it.
issues.correction: It tested the program's own contact-range gate on both sides. For particles the pull falls short by 10^28–10^31 (Debt 3a). For wave dark matter whose gate also makes dwarf cores, clumping would be mandatory in ultra-faint dwarfs and would drain them, which observation rules out (3b, 3c). With the coupling free, the record still allows streams, but at a tunable strength, so they predict nothing (Scenario B, quarantined). The obituary says clumping is nowhere required, not that it cannot occur.

overall:
The draft answers both of Paul's questions directly in its first section, after one short status paragraph. Neither answer is wrong, and I found no high-severity issue. That matches the critic's ruling that neither answer changes.

Every number I rechecked reproduces from the printed outputs. The check script and its output are in /home/paul/.claude/projects/-home-paul-git-reinholdtsen-conjugate-matter/7156ee3a-6166-4b9e-84c4-fb9703a50211/mg/answer-check-scope/ (scope_numbers.py, scope_numbers.out). The draft's statements about the record match the repository text: #11 §7 builds X as a spin-2 field on spacetime; #11 §8 tags the gate '[D — mechanism; shape [O]]'; #11 §14 item 4; #13 §2 'operates at F ~ c̃' against §5's 'free fall' as dual rest; the diameter note §8.2; verify/phase_space_diameter.py lines 383–384; the notebook §5.2 'anomalous velocity'; Debt 3a; flag 19. Flag 16 is relevant but not cited.

The real problems are scope and calibration:
- **Obituary scope.** The obituary is described only by its particle leg. The record's verdict is 'nowhere mandatory', and it keeps optional streams on the free-wave branch, which matters for 'premature'.
- **Up-front summary.** 'Too weak to clump' generalizes a ruling that the critic limited to 120 km/s.
- **Dropped qualifiers.**
  - The ε ≈ 3 exclusion holds in the force-law reading only; the record's reading is singular there.
  - Whether the Hamiltonian reading is the right limit for a long-range gate is open.
  - λ_X < 37.7 μm assumes u = 1 and no screening.
  - 'Only dependence on relative velocity' is too strong: flag 39's Siegel reading and #13's force-dual reading give other, negligible corrections.
  - The 264×/6500× margins rest on thresholds beyond the local model's validity; the robust margin is at least 6–9×.
  - 'Mildly prefer' for eBOSS understates a Δχ² of 24.

The deliberate departure, an uncomputed region at gates below 3 km/s, is justified. The corrected estimates start at 3 km/s, and the N-body never ran gates narrower than the dispersion. The departure is more accurate than the critic's own load-bearing summary, which says the remainder has ε < 1. Its threshold wording needs fixing: 'ε ≳ 10' conflicts with the draft's own 4.24, and both lie beyond the model's validity.

I could not confirm the draft's 'I checked' statements (Enander–Mörtsell, eq. 129) from the sources I was allowed to read; the critic attributes the Enander–Mörtsell check to a verifier and says it did not recheck it. The repository was not modified.
